title: Rust: variables that don't change
summary: let, mut, shadowing and integer sizes: what rustc refuses, and why.

text: In Rust, a variable can't change unless you say so.
- let: fixed. The compiler refuses any change.
- let mut: this one may change.
- Why? Reading the code, you know which values move. Fewer surprises.
A new let with the same name hides the old variable: that's shadowing.
- Unlike mut, the new variable can have another type.
- Handy to turn text into a number and keep a good name.
An integer type says its size: u is unsigned (0 and up), i can be negative, the number is the bits.
- A u8 holds 0 to 255. 250 + 10 doesn't fit.
- In a debug build, Rust stops (panics) instead of quietly wrapping to 4.
- When rustc can see both values, it refuses x + 10 before the program even runs.
A const is fixed forever, known when the program is built.
- Its type must be written: rustc doesn't guess it.
- The _ in 100_000 is only there to read it easily.
